correctness.rationale: A nonzero value f(lambda_i) creates an asymptotically constant row of the divided-difference symbol, giving a matrix-unit obstruction to compactness and an essential-distance lower bound. When f vanishes on the spectrum, the multiplier becomes a weighted finite-spectral pinching; Schatten Holder and the sharp exponent inequality give norm approximation by finite-rank maps in every index regime, including quasi-Banach endpoints.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The 2026 primary source gives the sharp boundedness region but no matching compactness classification was found in its inspected text. Older compact Schur multiplier, unequal-ideal multiplier, and quasi-Schatten literature was checked at available theorem/abstract level; no source located states the spectral equivalence for this divided-difference family across the full sharp region.

value.rationale: The result identifies a sharp qualitative boundary beyond the newly completed boundedness classification: compactness is equivalent to the rigid spectral condition f(H_lambda)=0. It also supplies a quantitative fixed-row essential-distance obstruction and a reusable weighted-pinching mechanism.
